solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

E022-01.notes: Object of 'assigned' needs objective case: 'my partner and me'. Hypercorrect 'I' sounds right to many; B reflexive lacks antecedent; D possessive wrong.

E022-02.notes: Narrative is past tense (Last fall, was, wrote down); 'visited' keeps consistency.

flags: minor: D 'with care and carefully' is an implausibly silly distractor

E022-05.notes: Nonrestrictive clause closes with a comma before 'was', so it must open with a comma; dash/comma mismatch in A; semicolon C fragments; D leaves clause unbalanced.

flags: minor: an empty position marker [] appears after Sentence 4 in this item's passage though the item is a sentence-placement question; harmless but stray
E022-06.notes: 'Then we checked each batch with him' must follow Sentence 3, which introduces the batches (cooked three times).

flags: Passage inconsistency: paragraph 3 says the soup was cooked three times and on the third try Mr. Okoye said 'Yes,' but this sentence says 'Of the two versions we tested, the second was ... faithful ... but even that one needed more ginger.' Two vs. three versions, and the 'needed more ginger' conclusion contradicts the approved third batch. Recommend revising the sentence (e.g., 'Of the first two versions we tested...') or the earlier paragraph.
E022-07.notes: Two items compared -> comparative 'the more faithful'. B is ungrammatical; C superlative without article.

flags: minor: list 'Mexico, Nigeria, Japan and Poland' omits the serial comma; ACT style accepts this but students might be distracted by it; also slightly odd that a single class's book is described only as 'four countries'
E022-08.notes: Colon after a complete independent clause introducing a list is correct; B comma makes 'Mexico' look appositive/ambiguous; C semicolon needs independent clause after; D no punctuation.
